items.claim: declare() takes its default `speed` from the live rate, not the spec's rate
reset() throws on a `start: 'end'` clock whose run has since become endless
items.note: I made the strict call: any `duration`, `loop`, `declare` or `override` that would make such a run endless now throws a `RangeError`. Reopening such a clock endless from a recorded position throws too. This is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`. One effect: labkit's transport loop toggle on a `start: 'end'` trial now throws from its click handler, where before it was `reset` that threw later.

items.claim: A ramp off 0 doesn't release a hold, so a later declare snaps the playing clock back
items.note: The hold now also watches frames and lets go on the first one that moves the clock.

items.claim: holdPosition maps an ended run's position to the end of the new run
holdPosition splits the recorded position into passes with a bare floor
items.note: B's example numbers don't show it (`500 * 0.1` is exactly 50 in JS). The defect is real for other values, though: `54.91691422425496 / 0.8448756034500764` rounds the pass up to 65. The test uses that case.

items.claim: holdPosition sends a recorded pass past the loop to the run's end instead of the last pass
items.note: A hold waits for a target its span can't reach yet ("A time past the pass's end waits at it"). The existing test "waits for a run long enough to reach it, then reaches it" pins this, and `pending` reports the target while it waits.

items.claim: PlayheadHold.pending says "clamped", but holdAt returns the raw `shown`
items.note: (doc only). The behavior was right and is pinned by tests, since the span may reach that time later. The doc now says what each kind of hold reports.

items.claim: A shadowed clock stops being synced, then jumps by the whole time away when it comes back : two parts
items.note:
`useClockLoop` rebases any clock that joins its entries, so a clock released and registered again doesn't jump.
  - fixed 9cb2723aa5: the registry's `all()` and `targets()` now include shadowed registrations, so a shadowed clock keeps playing. This was my call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`. I updated the model in `hold.pbt.test.ts` to match.
It adds a new public read, `Clock.ramping`, so that changeset is `minor`.

items.claim: `holdPosition` reads an ended position as a pass past the run
`declare` takes the default `speed` from the current rate instead of the declared one
`holdAt` and `holdPosition` give different `pending()` answers for a time past the pass end
A clock shadowed under its id jumps by the shadowed time when released
items.note: `useClockLoop` now rebases any clock that joins the loop.

items.claim: `reset()` throws on a `start: 'end'` clock whose run was made endless
items.note:
This needed a behavior call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md` under a new "Audit round thirty-seven" section:
  - Reset now goes to the end of the declared run instead of throwing.
  - `declare` now throws a `RangeError` on a declaration with no end for such a clock, and keeps the last declaration.

items.claim: `setDuration` to or from endless keeps a stale pass end, where `applyRun` clears it
`holdAt.pending` compares a float round trip instead of the elapsed it sought
items.note: The same old comparison sat in the oracles of `hold.pbt.test.ts` and `calls.pbt.test.ts`, and both now match.

items.claim: `calls.pbt.test.ts` asked for 20 "quiet" calls, more than its runs reliably reach. It failed about half the time on the unchanged frozen tree
`clock.pbt.test.ts` asked for 5 "seek:line" cases, but a random seek rarely lands on a pass line. It failed most runs on the frozen tree
items.note: (a new command now aims a seek at a pass line).
